memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "And he wept so loudly that the Egyptians heard him, and Pharaoh's household heard about it." — Gen 45:2 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Joseph sent everyone out of the room, but he could not send his grief far enough. He weeps so loudly that it carries through the walls, out into the corridors, all the way to Pharaoh's house.

Twenty years of held-back sorrow comes out at once. Everything he swallowed as a seventeen-year-old boy in a pit. Everything he could not say as a slave. Everything he buried in a prison cell. It has all been sitting there, and now it finally has somewhere to go.

Do not miss this: Joseph is the second most powerful man in the world, and he is sobbing on the floor. Strength and tears are not opposites. Some of the strongest people you will ever meet are the ones who have let themselves grieve properly.

Our Lord Jesus wept at a graveside (Jn 11:35), and He was not weaker for it. He was, in that moment, showing us the heart of God towards human sorrow. God has never asked us to be stoic. He collects our tears (Ps 56:8) and He has promised a day when He will personally wipe every one of them away (Rev 21:4).

If you have been holding something in for years, you are allowed to bring it to Him. He is not embarrassed by your tears.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Is there grief you have been holding in that you need to bring honestly to God?
2. Have you believed the lie that strong people do not cry?
3. What comfort do you find in knowing Jesus wept?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, I bring You the sorrow I have been carrying quietly. Thank You that You are not embarrassed by my tears but keep every one of them. Comfort me with the hope that one day You will wipe them all away. Amen.
